scenario_text: A mid-sized private bank currently runs its core banking system on a legacy COBOL framework. Management has decided to migrate the entire system to a modern Java-based framework. No new functionality is to be added — the migrated system must replicate the existing features exactly. Testing and validation is required at every stage of the migration to ensure nothing breaks. The project team consists of 2 developers and needs to be completed within 3-4 months.

justifications.gives_up: V-Shaped assumes an existing system is being extended — that is not the case here, so that part of its design earns nothing on this project.

sdlc.summary: The project's characteristics align with the V-Shaped model, making it the recommended choice. The project's requirements are well-defined, stable, and can be pinned down before build starts, and the project requires thorough testing and validation at every stage of the migration. The project's characteristics include a fixed delivery window, an approved scope, and a long-lived infrastructure, which all support the V-Shaped model. The project's need for formal verification and testing at multiple stages also aligns with the V-Shaped model's emphasis on finding defects early. The only mismatch is that the project is not an enhancement to an existing system, but this is not a critical factor in this case.
sdlc.shortcut: stable requirements + fixed delivery window + long-lived infrastructure -> V-Shaped
sdlc.cross_check_reasoning: The top choice, Waterfall, fits because it is a linear and sequential approach that allows for thorough testing and validation at every stage, which aligns with REQ-002. Additionally, Waterfall's focus on delivering a complete system at the end of the project cycle ensures that the system replicates the existing features exactly without any loss of functionality, aligning with REQ-003.

risk_register.title: High-risk function depends on an external system (REQ-001)
risk_register.cause: REQ-001 is high risk and classified Integration: The system shall be migrated from a COBOL framework to a Java-based framework
risk_register.consequence: An external system's availability, contract or interface change blocks a high-risk function.
risk_register.mitigation: Agree interface contracts early, stub the dependency for testing, and define fallback behaviour.

risk_register.title: Legacy migration — undocumented behaviour and data conversion
risk_register.cause: The problem statement says: "A mid-sized private bank currently runs its core banking system on a legacy COBOL framework."
risk_register.consequence: Behaviour the old system relied on is lost or data is converted wrongly.
risk_register.mitigation: Inventory existing behaviour, reconcile migrated data, and run old and new in parallel before cut-over.
evidence: A mid-sized private bank currently runs its core banking system on a legacy COBOL framework.

risk_register.consequence: The Java framework may not be compatible with the existing COBOL framework, leading to integration issues and potential system crashes.

risk_register.title: Insufficient testing resources
risk_register.cause: The problem statement says: "Testing and validation is required at every stage of the migration to ensure nothing breaks. The project team consists of 2 developers and needs to be completed within 3-4 months. The project team is small and the testing process is time-consuming, which may lead to insufficient testing resources to ensure the migrated system meets the required standards. The project team may not be able to test the system thoroughly within the given timeframe, which could lead to defects and errors in the migrated system."
